# Westernesse: consolidated open register

**Read as tickets and features (15 November).** `bun scripts/register-tickets.ts` places every row on a feature
(doc/architecture/features.json: what it is, the files it lives in, the specs that guard it) and says which rows are
live and how ready each is (ready, wants a decision, wants research, unverified). `--feature <id>` lists a feature's
live rows; `--touching <file>` says which features a changed file could touch and what is live there; `--unmapped`
lists rows with no feature. A new row must be placeable (its id in `rows`, or its prefix in `byPrefix`):
test/small/register-tickets fails with the row named.

**No row is partly (the owner, 20 November: "It's pretty binary in planning, isn't it? Either it was done or not. Items
don't need to be immutable; we can split off the undone work").** A row is open, closed (on the spec that proves it),
duplicate, deferred (on the owner's ruling) or reference. Work half done is split: the row closes on what its spec
proves, and the remainder becomes a row of its own ("split from X"), at the remainder's own priority. The rows still
marked partly are converted by the tribunal (Z0, first-hour rows first); test/small/register-tickets holds their count
and lets it only fall. Closed rows with a proof spec, read by someone other than their closer, move to the register's
archive (doc/architecture/register-archive.md, moved by `bun scripts/register-archive.ts --apply` on its rule), which
the readers read too. Old and settled rows move there apart, under headings that say so (20 November: "archive
old/solved defects"): a duplicate, and a row closed before proof specs were asked for, once older than the fortnight.

**Closing a row (the sprint audit's lesson, 19 November).** A row is closed (fixed, met, closed) only with one of:
a spec that tests the row's own claim, named in the status (not a neighbour that passes either way: barrow-forewarned
passed without the forewarning); or a stated reason it cannot be checked headless and what would prove it (a CI
browser recording, a human session). Someone other than its closer reads the spec against the claim before it
counts: another agent, or the lead reading an agent's. A closure on a code read or one walk alone is `partly`.
Directions and future scope (KX, SS, PG, SR, IM and their kind) are counted apart from defects; the burn-down that
matters is the first hour's live P0 and P1 rows (`bun scripts/register-tickets.ts`), with 2–3 blind plays at 7/10 or
more, before a human playtest (the owner, 19 November).

Compiled 11 November 2026, read-only, from the repository at `/var/tmp/kyrie/wt-m20` (main plus local commits through
`33cf0777`) and the owner's checkout for the risk review. A draft for the M20 handoff. It is not a disposition. It
claims nothing beyond what the sources say.

**Sources read**
- `doc/history/missions/20/`:
  - log.md: amendments 1–8, the open queue, rows E1–E133;
  - handoff.md (draft), text-inference.md, user-notes.md, opening-brief.md;
  - opportunities.md, design-opportunities.md, amendment-6.md, opening-design.md;
  - cold/round-1..6: every report's "Top five problems", and round 6's §4–§17 in full.
- `doc/history/missions/19/`: closure.md, register.md (all 297 rows), inherited.md (145 rows; it reconciles
  M18's wishlist, which itself carried M17 and M16).
- `doc/history/missions/17/ahead.md`; M18 register (OWN-07 only).
- `doc/history/findings/`:
  - index.md: confirms M16 → M17 → M18 → M18 wishlist → M19 inherited was carried id by id;
  - gaps.md / gaps.tsv: 74 UNT rows never registered;
  - briefs.md: 109 BRF requirements.
- The 9 November reviews (stabilization, quest-intent, throughput). Their recommendations were carried as
  M19-239..283, and are cited through those rows.
- 2026-11-11-adventure-to-career.md, headless-rpg-investigation.md, capability-audit.md.
- `/home/jweissman/work/kyrie/doc/history/missions/20/architecture-risk-mediation-2026-11-11.md` (R1–R10).
- Memory notes: all m20-*, owner-adventure-to-career, mission-20, and the m19-owner-*, m18-owner-* and mission-*
  descriptions. The open, next and remaining lines were found by grep.

**Not read line by line:**
- the M16, M17 and M18 registers row by row: the findings index shows their open rows were carried into M19's
  inherited ledger;
- M18 closure.md: its "Carried" items are BRF-56..65;
- the M13–M15 reports.

**How it was deduped.**
- One row per problem, citing every source id. Ids are:
  - E = M20 log;
  - R = risk review;
  - R*n*-X = cold round *n*, player X;
  - M19-/PD- = M19 register;
  - other prefixes (ARV, REV, OWN, PT, …) = M19 inherited;
  - UNT = findings gaps;
  - BRF = briefs;
  - H§ = handoff;
  - mem: = a memory note.
- A later record of a fix closes a row. Where the fix was partial, only the remainder is carried. Closed examples:
  - M19-233 by E2/E3;
  - M19-170 by E43/E79;
  - BRF-58 by E122.
- Status is as recorded, with its date. Where the newest source is older than 10 November it reads "unverified since
  <date>". Rows of the 9 November reviews and of the M19 closing audit (M19-239..283) are dated 10 November, the
  closure.
- Home is one of:
  - **M20 close**: only small first-hour defects, plus M20's own named gates;
  - **M21**;
  - **later**.

Nothing holds 'bosses dead in a round' or 'most players lost no hit point' today. **Measured and pinned 24 Nov (fights-1124: scripts/first-hour-fights.ts and first-hour-bands.ts, held by test/features/conflict/fights-cost.pin):** on the supported route (iscoed, the warrior and the hire Carlin), the golden walk meets one fight, the gate-well's conger (two rounds, two hit points lost, the company hit, the conger standing after the first round, won, reckoned fair beforehand); the gold-follower meets none (it stops after 14 steps at Redkeep's speaking door, the page leading with a thing it has nothing to do with). The 20 bands within 230 minutes of the start (Holyking's barrow, Deepwater's keeper, the raiders' ring-fort, Redkeep, the Numbered House), ten seeded trials each, fought by the warrior and Carlin whole: every one told as it goes (fair or slight won 9-10 in 10; the 7 grave or deadly kill the warrior in 5-10 of 10; hard won 8-10 with the warrior down in 0-3); in 17 of the 18 that stand the company is hit in most trials (the Gaffer: 4 in 10), median hit points lost 3 to 32 (the Gaffer's 0); every band's leader lives past the first round in at least half its trials, every lone one in 9 or 10 of 10; only the beasts of the wild (a fox, a butterfly) flee before a blow. So 'challenge 1-2, most lost no hit point, high-armour never hit, bosses dead in a round' no longer holds on this route, and no rules change was made: what the numbers show is frequency, not balance (one fight on the walk, none for the gold-follower). Closed (24 Nov) on its declared acceptance, by the opening's and the first dungeon's fights measured on the representative route (scripts/descent-fights.ts: the adit, then the reference journey under Porthalen by its rows, each fight as met and again over 40 seeded trials as the company stood, by calling). The warrior: the badger a bout that can be passed by (the page walk goes by it; a choice); the rats 4 hit points (5 rounds; hurt in 10 of 40 trials); the old buck none (9 rounds, its six bites needing 12 all missed; hurt in 14 of 40); the spider and the spiders' mother none in the walk but the warrior down in 7 and 8 of 40; the dead of the charnel passage 15 (5 rounds); the man with the black candle 2, said grave (down in 11 of 40); the goblin chief 34 (13 rounds, its parley offered beside it); the vault's keeper said grave and fatal in the walk (down in 20 of 40). A thief alone dies at the spiders' mother and at the man with the black candle, each said deadly (Beyond you) beforehand; a mage alone did not come past the adit's prop (below). One silent death found and mended: heaving the adit's fallen prop alone killed a mage come out of the badger's bout at two hit points of four, unasked and unwarned (OR-226). ## 28. The owner's planar grand tour (14 November, night)

The owner: a mage with Plane Shift goes to each inner and outer plane, and the specs assert each plane's laws read and act differently, as low-order as the architecture allows, with lazy generation and determinism in mind (travel to the Plane of Fire and take fire damage each turn; every elemental interaction present and resistible, blockable or wardable). Given to the rules line after the descent repair (completion plan §4).

Today a law is read only in combat and is ±1 spell DC; Earth, Water, Positive and Negative have none | open · progress (17 Nov): every inner plane has a law, and a law's onTurnEnd runs at the end of each turn in a fight (PlaceLaws) and each watch out of one on the company (PlaneLaws), through the damage pipeline: the Fire 1 fire (fireproof stops it), the Water 1 cold (waterproof), the Negative 1 necrotic (protected, darkproof), the Positive heals 1; the Earth judged (no harm, +1 DC), the Air no harm. ## 36. Empty words (the owner and the prose-density audit, 14 November)

Scope (the owner's brief), not defects found.

The audit is `history/reviews/prose-density-audit-2026-11-13.md`. The owner adds that empty words are an obstacle:
they make the game feel slower and more pointless. The long, detailed compound sentence is the engine's worst tic, and
a three-sentence budget does not catch it. Less text also helps performance at the limit.
- The measure is `src/presentation/clause-load.ts`. A heavy sentence passes 22 words or 3 joints.
- The terminal walks report the clause load of everything said unasked.
- `bun scripts/clause-census.ts [--first-hour]` is the editors' worklist.
- `test/small/clause-load` is the ratchet. It holds the first hour's heavy sentences at 1,256 of 7,275 (17.3 %). The
  whole authored corpus stands at 20.1 %.

## 46. The casting-fiction invariant (the owner, 15 November)

Causal legibility: who did this, by what learned capability, at what cost, under what rules, and what happened. A calling
grants education and vocabulary, an ability produces an effect, an authored action arranges circumstances and invokes
capabilities and never invents an unnamed power. Written up with the audit in
doc/architecture/mission-21/casting-fiction.md.

| Id | What | Status | Pri | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CF-01 | The invariant: every authored action that changes the world by magic resolves through a named ability, item, ritual, environmental mechanism or canonical calling technique, and its event keeps caster, means, source, targets, cost, attack/save/resistance results and effects, inspectable after reload. **Written and audited (15 Nov):** of 14 authored Slay/Restore actions (scripts/casting-audit), none invokes an ability, 4 hold and spend an item, 2 are gated on a calling alone, 8 have no named means (a rite, a spring and a battle among them, to review); 52 actions are gated on hasCalling/learned (51 assert a fact), unreviewed. Held as a ratchet that may shrink and not grow (test/small/casting-audit) | duplicate of CF-05 (20 Nov, tribunal): held: the audit as a ratchet, no new consequential action on a calling alone, bare ones at most 8 (test/small/casting-audit.test.ts:14-25, run: pass). The invariant itself is unmet: 0 of 13 invoke an ability, 8 bare (sallowfield's battle and arcs, tallow's lay_dead), 52 calling-gated unreviewed: CF-05 owns the 8 and the 52 and the lint, CF-02 the brood's fire, CF-04 the items' own effects, CF-03 a band as a target. The event's record (caster, means, source, targets, cost, results) inspectable after reload is to be asked by CF-05's review | P1 | M21, rules |
| CF-02 | The undertown's `_u_rats_slept` ("a mage's charm, not the Sleep spell") and `_u_brood_spelled` ("a magician's fire"): a calling alone, free, no bound caster, no area, save, resistance or Hit Dice limit, `Slay` outright (sleep and kill conflated), a power no canon, handbook or forecast names. **Acceptance (the owner):** a mage without Sleep is not offered it; one who can cast it is named, and Sleep by its canonical name; the same cost and the same target, save, resistance and duration rules as elsewhere; caster, spell, targets and results recorded; resisters stay active; sleepers are asleep, not dead; killing them is a distinct action; save/reload keeps it; terminal, browser, forecast and handbook agree | fixed (16 Nov): `_u_rats_slept` is "Have {caster} cast Sleep over the rats in the run": canCast(caster, sleep), Resolve invoke(sleep, caster, rats) (CF-03's route: the slot, each rat's save), what resists or wakes comes at the company (assails); "Do for the sleeping rats where they lie" is a separate act (Resolve combat when not able and not dead); the job rule clears on dead, or not able and not lulled, so sleeping rats are not cleared; the laboratory's Lowmouth the same. | BX-02 | The shared rules cannot be taken in part: a world of its own must install the whole standard set (data/rules: core, passages, people, needs, services, discovery, care, belongings, dominion, probing, inhabitants, growing, making, belief, ambitions), because they read one another. `core` alone has no kind of passage (passages.kyr's); `people` (talk), `belongings` and `inhabitants` read `hostile`, which is `dominion`'s (conflict and rule over places). So a civic scenario (the allotment society, BX-01) carries 97 shared actions, 58 rules and the catalog's abilities it never uses, and a fight's machinery under its talk. Wanted: the shared rules as packages with declared dependencies (a kernel of places, ways, people and talk that reads nothing of conflict), each installable alone, checked by a spec that installs each package with only what it declares; the allotment society then on the kernel alone | the separation proof's census, 24 November (the lead: the allotment world under smaller rule sets fails to load: 'Unknown kind passage' on core alone, 'Unknown function or arity: hostile(?p, ?c)' on core with people, services, discovery, needs, care and belongings) | open (24 Nov; the kernel stands alone, 24 Nov: core, passages, people and discovery install with nothing else, and the allotment society plays through on them, 114 entities, 34 actions and 11 rules where the standard set had 559, 97 and 58 (test/small/boundary-allotment). The causes: what every world's people, things and knowledge are (member, item, itemkind, fact; memberOf, awake, itemKind, ownedItem, knows, hostile) had been declared in care, belongings, discovery and dominion, now in core, their rules where they were; and the engine wrote or read ten relations of the other packages without asking whether the world declares them (wearing, treatable, canCast, needsCare in CreatureFacts; madeWhole, struckDead, handed, usesUp in Consequences; sells, soldBy in TradeModel), each now only where declared. The cold captures replay to the same digests. Left: core still declares the two acts of conflict (attack, assail), which the engine assumes in some fifty places; the other packages are not yet installable alone, nor checked so; the catalog's abilities still stand in every world) | P1 | M22-beta, maturity, separation |

| OR-423 | The player knows too much: the first person a new life meets offers some seventeen specific questions, most implying people, places, incidents and mysteries the character has never met (a cold play's finding; the owner, 25 November: "there are too many conversation topics available without any investigation"). Wanted: a topic is open only on the character's own knowledge (observation, testimony, reading, exploration, background, an earlier talk), a new life beginning with a few broad, natural questions; what is true kept apart from what a character knows, believes or suspects (a rumour lets a question be asked without making it fact); the prerequisites the engine's, in Kyr and the offered acts' legality, never inferred by a client from a topic's words | the owner's playtest and a cold play, 25 Nov | closed (25 Nov, re-landed): toldMatter(them, company) (data/rules/discovery.kyr), asserted by "Ask X what the matter is in <town>" (src/world/town-matters.ts) and by reading the notice on the green; the town's particular topics wait on it, a town's job on it, the notice or having been there (OR-370). The two leads that had pointed past the gate open on what they teach: the pans trader's "why the pans are cold" on the one smoking chimney or the cold (the golden walk's day-one pin), the drain's question on having been in the drain, the dead man's last night on the bruise the death's aim begins with; test/small/led-question-askable holds it over every askedOf and aim in data/. Seed c3's round was the dark: the candle burned out in the undercroft on the long way round through the catacombs, and the worn rats' path at the warren, a sign, was never seen, so the rats job's way was never learnt; the run is now heard in the dark as well (test/small/rats-heard-dark), and test/no-lead-round passes on all twelve seeds. ## 58. Stories, not situations (the owner, 18 November: the structural and literary critique)

The owner's critique of the standing scenarios (doc/architecture/reviews/scenario-structural-literary-critique-2026-11-18.md): "Kyrie often confuses a situation with a story, a task chain with an arc, branching
solutions with dramatic choice, and persistence with consequence." Its six tests (vector, revision, pressure, agency,
collision, aftermath) and its revision protocol (the seven sentences, the scene budget, the branch and clock tests) are
the measure. The golden route's sequence comes first (Sprint 2: ST-01..ST-04).

| Id | What | Status | Pri | When |
